recipes.name: Sweet and Sour Pork Tenderloin
ingredients_raw: 1 (1 1/4 pound) pork tenderloin, trimmed of silver skin
1 (8 ounce) can pineapple chunks, drained with juice reserved
2 teaspoons hot chili sauce (such as Sriracha®)
0.25 cup chopped green onion (white part only)

steps.text: Cut tenderloin into 4 pieces. Arrange in a single layer between two sheets of plastic wrap and pound with a meat mallet until each is about 1-inch thick. Generously season with salt and black pepper.
Whisk ketchup, rice vinegar, reserved pineapple juice, brown sugar, garlic, hot chili sauce, soy sauce, and red pepper flakes in a bowl. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over high heat. Place pork in pan; reduce heat to medium. Cook until browned on both sides and cooked through, 5 to 6 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
Return skillet to medium heat. Stir butter into hot pan. When butter melts and starts to brown, stir in pineapple chunks. Cook, stirring, until pineapple is golden brown, 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir in ketchup mixture and 1/4 cup green onion (white parts). Reduce heat to low and simmer until garlic and onion have softened, 5 minutes.
Return pork to skillet; cook, stirring, until pork is heated through. Garnish with 2 tablespoons green onion tops.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet and Sour Pork Tenderloin
raw_recipe.description: Chef John's sweet and sour pork with pineapple and green onions is a lighter version of the Chinese take-out classic.

review.reviewBody:
A very tasty meal. The only change I made was to saute some carrot, onion, and Green pepper
after removing the pork and before adding the pineapple--reserving the veg, adding back in once the fruit was carmelized.
I made this dinner for two, and the amount of sauce was adequate. You may wish to increase the sauce ingredients for four.

Loved the sauce! I doubled the amounts for the sauce and added more veggies. I put my black iron skillet with some olive oil on my outdoor grill and preheated it all up. I cooked the meat as directed After removing the meat, I added four sliced carrots, cut in thick strips, layered several small red yellow and orange peppers, onions, snow peas and fresh mushrooms (all cut in nice chunks) and put the pineapple on top. I let the carrots sit on the bottom of the hot skillet for about five minutes before stirring all the veggies and continued cooking for about five more minutes. Add a little butter if needed. I added the sauce as directed, cooked and returned meat to pan to heat through. I served it over basmati rice. Very good. I will make this again. I think it would also be good with shrimp.

Gets 3 stars AFTER making changes to recipe, mostly to exclude heat.

While the tenderloin comes out moist, tender, and edible -- if you cut it up into bite size pieces after browning -- there's too much heat in this recipe and not enough flavor or textural interest.

Try the following, so you can feed it to children.

Brown the meat on one side. In order to add flavor to meat, toss in garlic after it's flipped, 1-2 minutes before removing pork. Stir fry so garlic doesn't burn.

Be sure to wipe out and clean frying pan or wok thoroughly before adding butter/oil for stir-frying veggies.

Recommend altering recipe to include diagonally sliced carrot and cubed green pepper pieces. For added crunch, include water chestnut slices tossed in at the end of stir frying veggies.

Other changes: Substitute apple cider vinegar; sweet chili sauce; use no other spices; 1 Tbsp. cornstarch dissolved in 2 Tbsp. cold water added to sauce to thicken it. Stir, then pour over all ingredients as last step.

Served this delicious dish for company tonight! I used 1 1/2 pork tenderloins for 6 people and doubled the sauce but used a 20 oz can of pineapple. I also used sweet chili sauce in place of Sriacha. I added carrots, peppers, and onion as other viewers suggested. It was a hit served over rice with a tossed green salad and warm buttered Italian bread.

Added 1 tablespoon of corn starch to the liquids to thicken it. Cut the pork up into 1 inch pieces to cook faster. Didn't use the hot stuff. Used 1/4 cup chopped yellow onion
Will use twice the pineapple and liquids next time and put it over rice. This is a very easy and quite tasty recipe for pork tenderloin!

The sauce had great flavor and really made this recipe. I added yellow onion, green pepper, and celery chunks to the green onions to make this dish more hearty. I also added corn starch to the sauce to thicken it. Also doubled the sauce to have plenty to serve with rice. Substituted white wine vinegar that I had in the pantry for rice vinegar

Made the dish for 2 people using left over cooked pork tenderloin. Stir fried mix of veggies, peppers, onion, carrots, green beans then put them aside and followed the rest of the recipe adding them back in with the pork at the end. I made the sauce as with a few small changes. It was the perfect amount of sauce for 2. I would double the sauce for 4 as stated in another review. Only added 1 tsp of hot sauce and no pepper flakes it was just the right amount of heat for us. Also grated the 1 clove of garlic and some ginger into the sauce mix before cooking. Served over Jasmine rice it was delicious.

Awesome recipe! I added a jalapeños pepper (sliced), sautéed onions, carrots, and sweet bell peppers, to deglaze the saucepan with the pineapple chunks (I used fresh pineapple), sautéed them a bit before adding the sauce mixture. I also did a quick marinade of the pork tenderloin steak with salt, pepper, soy sauce, vegetable oil, soy sauce & corn starch, before pan searing them in step one. The heat was a bit too much for some members of my family so next time I will half the amount of jalapeños.

very good - I gave it a 4 because of some changes to recipe 
 I made --but the sauce is very good and it thickens on own w/ no cornstarch needed- I cut up a pork tenderloin into small chunks and added a sliced carrott , onion and peppers to it -
its a little spicy, so will cut the sriracha to 1 teasp & it needed more brown sugar- another heaping T... and was perfect will make it again . served over brown rice

Very tasty. For 2 tenderloin triple the sauce ingredients, except for two ingredients- sriracha ( use 1 Tbsp total) and pineapple (19 oz can is plenty). This provided just the right amount of spice. As per some other reviews, I did saute an onion, a few carrots, and a green pepper after taking the meat out, and then removed that, adding it back in with the meat. I sliced the tenderloin, and found the pieces still too big, so will cut into bite sized pieces next time. This will be my go to sweet and sour pork recipe, the family raved about it!

This was absolutely delicious and sauce was amazing... I added cornstarch on my pork before frying once done cut into pieces, followed this recipe and another from this site... Will definitely make again with any protein and muchore veggies, only had broccoli this time and the Onion
This was horrible. Im glad I tasted the sauce before I added the meat to it. I threw the sour sauce away.
Absolutely delicious. My only change was to cube the pork instead of pounding it out, and using sweet chili sauce instead of sriracha. I did add a bit more red pepper since we like the heat. Yummy!

Didn’t have green onions so used one slice of a yellow onion. My family doesn’t like spicy food so we eliminated the red pepper flakes and the hot chili sauce. added a bit of cornstarch to thicken the sauce. Served over MomoFuku Soy & Scallion noodles. Family loved it!!
I used pork tenderloin medallions. I substituted chili garlic sauce for the Sriracha and decreased the fresh garlic. Great flavor!
My family said the sauce would be better with chicken. I keep trying to find recipes for pork tenderloin and was excited for the possibility here but it just didn't work for us.
I used chicken and this was delicious!
I've made this several times over the past few years. It's not traditional sweet and sour but, still delicious, easy and not loaded with fat. Thanks Chef John!

Eyeballed the sauce measurements and still turned out great! After resting the pork, I sliced it before adding back to the pan and really enjoyed the final outcome. I think I will add some of our favorite stir fry veggies next time. Delicious recipe.

I added some chopped green peppers, chopped onions and chopped carrots after I removed the pork from the fry pan. When they were partly softened, I removed from the pan before adding the butter and pineapple. I added those veggies back in when I put in the sauce and pork (I cut into bitesize pieces while the veggies were cooking). I served it over Jasmine rice. Great recipe!
